quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and precipitation back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair driving. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, illegal drugs, and over-the-counter medicines like cough syrups, cold tablets, and allergy medications.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from that lane.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: You should change lanes:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully, only when needed. Each lane change increases your risk of an accident.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: Alcohol and drugs affect which driving skills?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, concentration, and coordination, and increases reaction time.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you is stopped with red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. You should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they conflict with traffic signs, signals, or markings.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, always wear a seat belt.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Wear the seat belt only behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags protect you in crashes, but they work best with seat belts. Always wear your lap and shoulder belts together with airbags for the best protection.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right and you need to turn right too. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish its turn before you turn.
Squeeze your car between the truck and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish its turn before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you make your turn.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or sign tells you to stop.
You have the right of way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or sign tells you to stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Always be careful when driving near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Drink caffeine.
Eat fatty foods.
Wait for time to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your blood alcohol level. Nothing else, like eating or drinking coffee, will speed up this process. Your body needs time to remove the alcohol.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for road conditions.
Getting plenty of rest and staying alert.
Watching your surroundings and paying attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than the speed limit or too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always follow the speed limit and drive at a safe speed for the road and weather conditions.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Challenge them.
Move out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to move out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not try to compete with other drivers. Always stay calm and respectful on the road.

questions.question: Before driving while taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor how the medicine affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Open your window and drive slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor how the medicine affects driving.
questions.explanation: Medicine can affect your driving ability. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine will affect your driving, especially prescriptions for tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as far. Poor visibility makes it difficult to judge how far away objects are and how fast other cars are going. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it off the road and away from traffic if possible. Turn on your emergency lights so other drivers can see that you have a problem.

questions.question: You see lowered railroad crossing gates and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then go when the gates are up.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates. Wait for the tracks to clear. Then go when the gates are up.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at lowered railroad gates. It is illegal to drive around them. Wait until the gates are raised and the tracks are clear before you proceed.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Make you a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Harm your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harm your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and harms your judgment.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if pedestrians are not texting while walking.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrians or vehicles cross. You may proceed carefully only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: If you see animals near the roadway while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Quickly move to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive carefully if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely follow the curves.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you there faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving choices.
